title: Monday Morning Quarterback (on Sunday)
date_line: Sunday, Nov. 22, 2026. College Saturday review: the Nov. 21 slate, graded as the games went final. Then what's next.

paragraphs: Saturday put 58 games on the card, and 53 of them are final and graded below. Five late games are still being played: Utah at TCU, San Diego State at Boise State, Oklahoma State at Arizona State, Utah State at Oregon State and Hawai'i at Nevada. They stay pending, and they get graded here in the next update once ESPN has the finals.

It was a night for the half-point and the last-second score. The Over 49.5 at Penn State died at 49 when Rutgers won 25-24 on a two-point play with no time left. SMU +20.5 lost by half a point because Notre Dame ran out the clock with kneel-downs. The Under 47.5 at Texas missed by half a point at 48, and the Under 54.5 at Marshall missed by half a point when Georgia State scored with 2 seconds left. Southern Miss +4.5 lost by half a point after its two-point try failed, Old Dominion scored with 1 second left to take 5.5 points off UConn −13.5, and Navy scored with 15 seconds left to beat Memphis −2.5 outright.

The other side of the window had its moments too. Kansas State +7.5 cashed by half a point in overtime, Maryland +17.5 and the Under 56.5 both cashed with the last point scored at 56, and Chattanooga +48.5 cashed when Alabama stopped at 47. Wake Forest −21 landed exactly on the number, and five tickets got their money back. BYU at Kansas went three overtimes and UCLA at Michigan went three overtimes, and Colorado State climbed back from 22 down to cash +20.5.

Every game below is graded against the line printed on the card at kickoff, using ESPN finals and play-by-play, and a push counts as neither a hit nor a miss. Saturday's cards were refreshed on game day, and Lock It Up line moves count at their final lines. The heartbreakers go first, then the nail-biters, then the rest of the card, then the five games still being played.
Follow The Money had a side in 14 of the graded games and a total in 25, and In The Trenches had a side in 27 and no totals. Games without a pick aren't graded for them.

Card line: UConn −13.5, total 47.5. The Cover Writer's card had UConn −13.5 and the Over, projecting UConn 33, Old Dominion 18. Final: Old Dominion 21, UConn 29. UConn won by 8, and the teams scored 50 points.

UConn −13.5 had this one in the bag, and Old Dominion took 5.5 points back with one second left. Baker's 34-yard field goal at 2:24 made it 29-14, a 15-point lead and a cushion of 1.5 over the number. Then Potter threw 6 yards to Haughton for a touchdown with 1 second on the clock. UConn won 29-21, and the win was 8 points, not 14.
That same snap kept the Over 47.5 alive and cashed it. The total sat at 43 with a couple of minutes left, and the final touchdown made it 50. One play, one ticket torn up and one ticket cashed.
Called it: The Formula on Old Dominion +13.5, covered by 5.5 points. The Formula, Next Man Up and Letdown Watch on the Over 47.5, cleared it by 2.5 points.
Called it: The Cover Writer on the Over 47.5, cleared it by 2.5 points.
Missed: The Cover Writer, Next Man Up and Letdown Watch on UConn −13.5, missed by 5.5 points.

Card line: South Alabama −4.5, total 66.5. The Cover Writer's card had Southern Miss +4.5 and the Under, projecting South Alabama 32, Southern Miss 30. Final: South Alabama 40, Southern Miss 35. South Alabama won by 5, and the teams scored 75 points.

South Alabama −4.5 won it, and Southern Miss +4.5 died by half a point on a two-point try. Davenport's 13-yard touchdown throw at 13:23 of the fourth cut it to 29-26, then Martin ran 50 yards for a touchdown at 7:48 to take the lead, 33-29, and 6 yards for another at 1:57, 40-29. Southern Miss answered with Sanders's 45-yard touchdown catch from White at 0:53, and the two-point throw failed. That left it 40-35, five points, and every Southern Miss +4.5 ticket needed one more point.

After the onside kick, South Alabama had the ball and kneeled three times, at the Southern Miss 48, the Southern Miss 50 and the South Alabama 49, to finish it. The Over 66.5 was never in danger at 75 points.
Called it: Letdown Watch on South Alabama −4.5, covered by 0.5 points. Next Man Up and Follow The Money on the Over 66.5, cleared it by 8.5 points.

Missed: The Cover Writer, The Formula, Next Man Up and In The Trenches on Southern Miss +4.5, missed by 0.5 points. The Cover Writer, The Formula and Letdown Watch on the Under 66.5, went over by 8.5 points.
Card line: Memphis −2.5, total 67.5. The Cover Writer's card had Memphis −2.5 and the Under, projecting Memphis 33, Navy 29. Final: Memphis 34, Navy 38. Navy won by 4, and the teams scored 72 points.

Memphis −2.5 led 34-24 with 12:38 left on Carter's 1-yard touchdown run, with a 10-point lead and 7.5 points of cushion. Navy came back from there. Gutierrez ran 68 yards for a touchdown at 6:57, 34-31, and then Listorti ran 6 yards for the winning touchdown with 15 seconds left. Navy 38, Memphis 34.

The Under 67.5 was sitting at 65 points after the long run and went over by 4.5 on the last touchdown. Four voices had Memphis −2.5 and the Under, and they all went down in the last seven minutes. The only winner on the board was Follow The Money on Navy +2.5 and the Over.
Called it: Follow The Money on Navy +2.5, covered by 6.5 points. Follow The Money on the Over 67.5, cleared it by 4.5 points.

Missed: The Cover Writer, The Formula, Next Man Up and Letdown Watch on Memphis −2.5, missed by 6.5 points. The Cover Writer, The Formula, Next Man Up and Letdown Watch on the Under 67.5, went over by 4.5 points.

Card line: Notre Dame −20.5, total 56.5. The Cover Writer's card had SMU +20.5 and the Under, projecting Notre Dame 37, SMU 18. Final: SMU 3, Notre Dame 24. Notre Dame won by 21, and the teams scored 27 points.

Notre Dame −20.5 won by 21, and SMU +20.5 lost by half a point. The Irish were up 24-3 after Notre Dame's James ran 4 yards for a touchdown at 11:31 of the third, and then nobody scored again. Notre Dame ran the clock from its own 12, got to its own 31, and closed the game with kneel-downs at its own 30 and its own 29. That is a 21-point win and a half-point cover.
The Under 56.5 was never in doubt at 27 points.
Called it: Next Man Up and Letdown Watch on Notre Dame −20.5, covered by 0.5 points. The Formula and Letdown Watch on the Under 56.5, stayed under by 29.5 points.
Called it: The Cover Writer on the Under 56.5, stayed under by 29.5 points.
Missed: The Cover Writer and The Formula on SMU +20.5, missed by 0.5 points. Next Man Up on the Over 56.5, fell 29.5 points short.

Card line: Penn State −26.5, total 49.5. The Cover Writer's card had Rutgers +26.5 and the Over, projecting Penn State 37, Rutgers 16. Final: Rutgers 25, Penn State 24. Rutgers won by 1, and the teams scored 49 points.

Rutgers 25, Penn State 24 is the upset of the night, and it still cost the Over by half a point. Penn State led 24-10 after Becht's 6-yard touchdown run at 4:57 of the third, and Raymond's 13-yard touchdown run at 10:19 of the fourth made it 24-17. Rutgers got into scoring range on two interference penalties against Penn State. Surace threw 3 yards to Black for the touchdown with no time left, and the two-point conversion throw to Gilley worked. Rutgers won by one as a 26.5-point underdog.

Rutgers +26.5 cashed by 27.5, and the Over 49.5 finished at 49 points, half a point short. Had Rutgers kicked the extra point instead of going for two, the total would have been 48. The Under 49.5 holder had the right ticket.
Called it: The Formula and Next Man Up on Rutgers +26.5, covered by 27.5 points. Follow The Money on the Under 49.5, stayed under by 0.5 points.
Called it: The Cover Writer on Rutgers +26.5, covered by 27.5 points.

Missed: Letdown Watch on Penn State −24.5, missed by 25.5 points. Follow The Money on Penn State −26, missed by 27 points. The Cover Writer, The Formula and Next Man Up on the Over 49.5, fell 0.5 points short. Letdown Watch on the Over 50.5, fell 1.5 points short.

Card line: Texas −20.5, total 47.5. The Cover Writer's card had Arkansas +20.5 and the Under, projecting Texas 32, Arkansas 13. Final: Arkansas 3, Texas 45. Texas won by 42, and the teams scored 48 points.

The Under 47.5 died by half a point at 48 points, and the half-point came in the fourth quarter of a blowout. Texas was up 38-3 on Terry's 1-yard touchdown run at 10:13 of the third, 41 points on the board. Cooper's 8-yard touchdown run at 7:31 of the fourth made it 45-3, 48 points, and that was it. Arkansas had kicked a 30-yard field goal back in the first quarter, and that 3 points was the whole difference.
Arkansas +20.5 lost by 21.5, and McDonald's 31-yard interception return for a touchdown at 9:01 of the first had it dead early.
Called it: Next Man Up on Texas −20.5, covered by 21.5 points. The Formula and Letdown Watch on the Over 47.5, cleared it by 0.5 points.
Missed: The Cover Writer, The Formula and Letdown Watch on Arkansas +20.5, missed by 21.5 points. The Cover Writer and Next Man Up on the Under 47.5, went over by 0.5 points.

Card line: Marshall −2.5, total 54.5. The Cover Writer's card had Georgia State +2.5 and the Under, projecting Georgia State 28, Marshall 24. Final: Georgia State 27, Marshall 28. Marshall won by 1, and the teams scored 55 points.

Georgia State +2.5 cashed, and it took the Under 54.5 down at the buzzer. Marshall led 28-21 on Del Rio-Wilson's 2-yard touchdown run at 6:30. Georgia State took over at its own 24 with 43 seconds left and Pereira hit Dorsey for a 31-yard touchdown with 2 seconds left. The extra point failed, so Marshall held on 28-27, but the total went to 55, over the Under 54.5 by half a point. One snap and one touchdown cashed the Georgia State +2.5 ticket by 1.5 and sank the Under.
Marshall took one knee after the onside kick to finish the game.

Called it: The Formula and Next Man Up on Georgia State +2.5, covered by 1.5 points. Letdown Watch on Marshall +1.5, covered by 2.5 points. Next Man Up on the Over 54.5, cleared it by 0.5 points. Letdown Watch on the Under 57.5, stayed under by 2.5 points. Follow The Money on the Under 55.5, stayed under by 0.5 points.
Called it: The Cover Writer on Georgia State +2.5, covered by 1.5 points.
Missed: Follow The Money on Marshall −2.5, missed by 1.5 points. The Cover Writer and The Formula on the Under 54.5, went over by 0.5 points.

Card line: Ohio State −3, total 41.5. The Cover Writer's card had Ohio State −3 and the Over, projecting Ohio State 27, Nebraska 21. Final: Ohio State 28, Nebraska 31. Nebraska won by 3, and the teams scored 59 points.

Ohio State −3 lost outright, and four voices had it. Ohio State led 7-0 early, then Nebraska ran off 21 straight, with Colandrea running for a 13-yard touchdown at 4:12 of the second to make it 21-7. Ohio State tied it at 21 on Jackson's 1-yard run at 6:37 of the third, and Nebraska's Colandrea hit Clark for a 26-yard touchdown at 7:41 of the fourth, 31-21. Jackson's 1-yard touchdown run at 3:52 made it 31-28, and Nebraska ran the clock down to a kneel-down at 0:28. Ohio State missed by 6 points against the spread. The Over 41.5 was the consolation, cleared by 17.5.

Card line: Northwestern −2.5, total 41.5. The Cover Writer's card had Northwestern −2.5 and the Over, projecting Northwestern 27, Minnesota 21. Final: Northwestern 17, Minnesota 20. Minnesota won by 3, and the teams scored 37 points.

Northwestern −2.5 lost by 5.5 on a field goal with 1 second left. Minnesota led 17-10 in the fourth, and Marchiol ran 7 yards for the tying touchdown at 0:27. Lindsey then hit Jennings for 34 yards to the Northwestern 33, and Drzewiecki kicked a 44-yard field goal with 1 second left. Minnesota 20, Northwestern 17.

Indiana −7.5 lost in overtime, and the Over 43.5 cashed on the tying touchdown. Indiana led 24-17 on Hoover's 35-yard touchdown throw at 9:06. Williams hit DeGraaf for 20 yards at 3:34 to tie it at 24. In overtime, Robles kicked a 46-yard field goal for Washington, 27-24. Wake Forest −21 landed exactly on the number, and five tickets got their money back. Georgia Tech's Knowles ran 7 yards for a touchdown at 2:42 and made it 50-29, and that was a 21-point game. Wake Forest recovered the onside kick, ran the clock, and kneeled three times to end it. A push for The Cover Writer, The Formula, Next Man Up and In The Trenches on Georgia Tech +21, and a push for Letdown Watch on Wake Forest −21.

Kansas State +7.5 cashed by half a point in overtime, and the Over 52.5 cashed with room to spare. Kansas State led 28-20 on a fumble recovered in the end zone at 10:55. Arizona's Fifita threw 35 yards to Mizell at 1:52, and the game was tied at 28. Arizona got the ball first in overtime and Fifita threw 25 yards to Richardson, 35-28. Kansas State needed a touchdown and could not get in from the Arizona 3, and the drive ended in a turnover on downs.
Arizona won by 7 and Arizona −7.5 missed by half a point, and The Cover Writer and In The Trenches cashed on Kansas State +7.5. The Over was no problem at 63 points.

San José State +6.5 cashed by 4.5 on a touchdown with 45 seconds left, and it cost the Over 47.5 a chance at a tie-breaking two-point try. UNLV led 24-13, and San José State's Sinatra kicked a 27-yard field goal at 6:51, 24-16. Weaver threw 30 yards to Clark for a touchdown at 0:45 and the two-point throw failed. UNLV 24, San José State 22. UNLV then took two knees at the San José State 45 and 48.
The Over 47.5 finished at 46 points. The failed two-point try was a 2-point play that would have made it 48.

hits.heading: Part 1, continued: The week's W-L and smack talk

paragraphs: The Cover Writer went 28-24-1 against the spread and 22-31 on totals Saturday, which makes the week 31-33-1 against the spread and 30-35 on totals. The sides finally woke up, with Rutgers +26.5 and Chattanooga +48.5 in the bank, and the totals fell into a ditch. The Over at Penn State, the Under at Texas and the Under at Marshall each died by half a point. Three half-points on one card is not bad luck, it is a personal attack, and The Cover Writer is taking it personally.

The Formula went 18-30-1 against the spread and 28-21 on totals Saturday, and for the week it is 23-37-1 against the spread and 36-25 on totals. The totals are the best in the building. Its Over 47.5 at Texas cashed by half a point and Georgia State +2.5 cashed on the last-second touchdown, but SMU +20.5 and Southern Miss +4.5 each died by half a point. The totals side is carrying the whole operation, and the sides owe it dinner.

Next Man Up went 19-29-1 against the spread and 22-27 on totals Saturday, and the week is 24-36-1 against the spread and 30-31 on totals. It cashed Notre Dame −20.5, Texas −20.5 and Rutgers +26.5, and it pushed Wake Forest +21. Then it lost Memphis −2.5, Ohio State −3 and Houston −7. Friday's big night is a long way back in the rearview mirror.

Letdown Watch went 24-24-1 against the spread and 23-26 on totals Saturday, and the week is 28-32-1 against the spread and 30-31 on totals. It was the only voice on Wake Forest −21 and pushed it with everyone else, and it cashed Notre Dame −20.5 and South Alabama −4.5 by half a point each. It also took Penn State −24.5 and watched Rutgers win the game. The letdown it keeps warning everybody about showed up in State College and nowhere else.

Follow The Money went 7-7 against the spread and 11-14 on totals Saturday, and the week is 10-10 against the spread and 13-17 on totals. It was the only voice on Navy +2.5 and the Over at Navy, and both cashed on the last touchdown, and it cashed the Over at Southern Miss too. Marshall −2.5 and Penn State −26 were the two that bit back. It sat out most of the card and picks its spots, and the spots were about even.

In The Trenches went 20-6-1 against the spread and made no total picks Saturday, and the week is 25-9-1. That is the best sides record anyone has put up all week, and it is not close. It had Chattanooga, Maryland, Kansas State, Minnesota, San José State and Sam Houston on the right side, and it pushed Wake Forest with the rest of them. Six of its sides lost, and Southern Miss +4.5 missed by half a point. It has no totals picks, so nobody can drag it down with the rest of the room.

look_ahead.closing_sentence: Next week's college cards go up on the game pages at thecoverwindow.com once lines are set, and they get graded here once the games are final.

paragraphs: Thanksgiving week opens quietly. Tuesday, Nov. 24 has Kent State at Eastern Michigan and Miami (OH) at Western Michigan, both at 7 p.m. ET, and Thursday, Nov. 26 has TCU at Texas Tech at 8 p.m. ET.

Friday, Nov. 27 brings 13 games. Nebraska at Iowa, Mississippi State at Ole Miss, Tulsa at UTSA, Buffalo at Akron and Toledo at Ohio all kick at noon ET, Florida at Florida State is at 3:30 p.m. ET, Air Force at New Mexico is at 4:30 p.m. ET, and Texas at Texas A&M and Minnesota at Wisconsin are at 7:30 p.m. ET. West Virginia at Utah closes the day at 9 p.m. ET.

Saturday, Nov. 28 is rivalry day.
